title: Killis
summary: Killis is a Bridgehampton pond placename that survives in the modern Kellis Pond name. The pond is recorded, and its name is connected with a Native person who lived near the water, while also noting later spellings and family-name forms.
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for modern Kellis Pond in Bridgehampton based on USGS/GNIS topographic data; not an exact historical residence or boundary.
why_this_matters: Bearing the traditional Shinnecock family name Kellis, this Bridgehampton pond honors a specific Indigenous individual who maintained a home along its shores. Preserving such deeply personal place names permanently anchors Native family histories into the everyday geography of Long Island, ensuring these legacies are not erased by modern development.
history_content: The source uses Prime's history for the account that the pond took its name from an Indigenous man associated with the place. The name also continued locally in forms such as Kittis, Kelly, Kellie, and Kellis, linking a pond, nearby households, and Bridgehampton memory.
translation_content:
No secure linguistic translation is given for Killis. The same source treats the name as connected to a person and lists related spellings, including Kittis, Kelly, Kellie, and an early Kettle's Pond form. The modern mapped place is Kellis Pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“I have always had an aversion to English place names. They mean nothing to the people who live there.”

— Michael Kusugak, Nunannguaq (2018), Capturing the Character of Our Land section
land_loss_content: Killis shows how Native names could remain attached to small local water places and family histories, even when later spellings shifted. Recording the pond with its variants helps preserve a Bridgehampton placename that might otherwise appear only as a modern road or property name.
whereintheworld_content: The point for modern Kellis Pond in Bridgehampton identifies the pond area, not a specific historic residence or boundary.
